hints.title: Examine First Two Edges
hints.text: The center node must be incident to every edge in the graph, so it must appear in both edge 0 and edge 1.

hints.title: Compare Endpoints
hints.text: Check which node is common between edges[0] and edges[1].

hints.title: Return Common Vertex
hints.text: If edges[0][0] matches either endpoint of edges[1], it is the center; otherwise edges[0][1] is the center.

hints.title: Full Implementation
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def findCenter(self, edges: list[list[int]]) -> int:
        u1, v1 = edges[0]
        u2, v2 = edges[1]
        return u1 if u1 == u2 or u1 == v2 else v1
```

complexity.whyNaiveFails: Counting degrees of all n nodes takes O(n) when inspecting 2 edges suffices in O(1).
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate inspects common element between first two edges in O(1) time.
